summary: Prepare fix plan for spike-timed steering and adversarially vetted new SNN+NEAT topics (read-only)

proposals.title: v3 search fix: mirror-tied antagonist-pair NEAT with a sparse start and gentle mutation, then a 4-knob calibration with the same budget as the classical law
proposals.diagnosis:
Conclusion: v1 learned only one direction because of a search failure, not a capacity or physics limit. About 75% of its J gap is the missing direction and about 25% is missing calibration.

Evidence (artifacts/spike_steer/v1; pulse signs from replaying the RNG in pilot.pulse_sign() in numpy, no simulation run):

(1) The x-sign of the stress disturbance (pulse_sign[0]) alone sets the dominant pitch need. On all 16 test cases:
- x=+1: the IMU law fires 87.5% up.
- x=-1: the IMU law fires 62% down.

The SNN result splits the same way, 16/16:
- x=-1 (down is enough): the SNN is close to the law. Pitch RMS 3.50 vs 3.18 deg, J 7.46 vs 6.53.
- x=+1 (up is needed): the SNN fails. Pitch RMS 5.99 vs 2.88 deg, J 8.88 vs 6.04.

So most of the gap (8.17 vs 6.29) is directional. The rest is calibration: even on x=-1 cases the SNN pays more height error (13.2 vs 11.2 cm) for less pitch correction.

(2) The second direction was within reach, and the training signal for it was present:
- Pulse authority is antisymmetric to within about 10%: +2.70/-2.46 rad/s at 135/315 deg, +2.74/-2.52 at 180/0 deg.
- One LIF readout can OR two phase x sign conjunctions.
- 18 of 20 v1 batches contained an x=+1 case (mean 1.6 of 3).

(3) The search could not build a second coordinated conjunction without breaking the first:
- Compatibility 3.0 gave one species for all 20 generations.
- Top-30% truncation plus elitism collapsed the population onto the first push-down lineage.
- Each child perturbed about 51 of 85 weights (rate 0.6, sigma 0.2).
- Each child also shifted about 25 delays with sigma 3 ms, about 27 deg of wingbeat. delay_mutate_power silently falls back to the gene default of 3.
- Each child reset about 2.5 delays to 0, because delay_replace_rate is 0.03 and the default init is 0 +- 0.

(4) Calibration is missing:
- The law's 4 knobs are tuned on a grid. The SNN's equivalents (input gains, threshold, pulse width) are spread over about 85 isotropically mutated genes.
- The champion is the winner of a 3-case batch. The generation-19 champion over-fired: validation height 19.6 cm, duty 5.1%.

What v2 may still miss. Balanced batches fix the batch composition (2 cases with x=+1, 2 with x=-1), but three problems remain:

(a) Both motor neurons read the same dense hidden layer, so nothing makes one specialise in pushing up. The push-up conjunction still has to be found by the same disruptive mutation.

(b) Compatibility 0.6 creates too many species. The live log shows 6 -> 10 species by generation 5.
- With elitism 2 per species and min_species_size 2, 20 of 32 genomes are unchanged elites. Only about 12 are new per generation, and each species breeds from its top 2.
- Species cannot die before max_stagnation=15.
- At 17 or more species, neat-python raises RuntimeError in _adjust_spawn_exact (32 < 17x2).

(c) There is still no calibration stage. Even a champion that pushes both ways can trail a law tuned on a 108-point grid.
changes:
Mirror-tied phenotype (/home/robot/FlapSim-repo/FlapSim/experiments/algorithms/spike_steer/pilot.py):
- Add MIRROR = (4,5,6,7,0,1,2,3,9,8,11,10): the input-index map phase cell +180 deg, th+ <-> th-, q+ <-> q-.
- Add MIRROR_OFFSET = 100_000.
- Add mirror_spec(spec). It appends a copy of every node (id + offset) and every edge. An input source -(i+1) becomes -(MIRROR[i]+1); node ids get + offset. It also adds the mirrored motor neuron(s) to 'outputs'.
- export(g) returns mirror_spec(...) when the new flag --mirror is set.
- The NEAT genome keeps num_outputs = 1: it encodes one motor pool, and the antagonist pool is derived from it.
- SpikingGraph, Steer.step (fire = any output) and the onset bookkeeping (which = 0 original, 1 mirror) work unchanged.

Sparse 'AND-gate' start: new initialize_sparse(pop, cfg, seed, hidden=4), selected with --init sparse (dense keeps v1's initialize).
- Each of 4 hidden LIF units reads ONE random phase cell (weight U(0.4,0.7), delay U{0..8} ms) and ONE random error channel from th+, th-, q+, q- (weight U(0.3,0.8), delay U{0..4}).
- Hidden bias N(0.3,0.1). Readout to the motor neuron N(2.0,0.5): a single hidden spike at spike_scale 5 raises the output voltage by about 0.5w, so w around 2 lets one conjunction spike start a twitch.
- Genome 0 keeps a zero readout (PID-only anchor).
- The half-genome has 5 nodes and 12 connections; v1 had 8 nodes and 85 connections.
- Pre-flight check (seconds, no simulation): feed SpikingGraph a synthetic sweep (phase bin x error 0..2). Confirm that at least 40% of fresh units fire only in their own bin above an error threshold; otherwise shift the bias mean.

New template neat_template_v3.ini next to neat_template.ini (gentle, fine-grained mutation):
- Weights: pop_size 40; weight_mutate_rate 0.6 -> 0.25; weight_mutate_power 0.2 -> 0.15; weight_replace_rate 0.02 -> 0.01; weight_init_stdev 0.6 -> 0.5.
- Biases: bias_mutate_rate 0.3 -> 0.2; bias_mutate_power 0.1 -> 0.05; bias_replace_rate 0.01 -> 0.
- Delays: add delay_init_mean = 4.0, delay_init_stdev = 2.0 and delay_mutate_power = 1.0 (currently the implicit 3 ms). Set delay_mutate_rate 0.3 -> 0.1 and delay_replace_rate 0.03 -> 0 (with the implicit init 0 +- 0 it currently snaps delays to 0).
- Structure: conn_add_prob 0.2 -> 0.3; conn_delete_prob 0.05 -> 0.1; node_delete_prob 0.03 -> 0.05; enabled_mutate_rate 0.01 -> 0.005.
- [DefaultReproduction]: elitism 2 -> 1; survival_threshold 0.3 -> 0.25; min_species_size 2.
- [DefaultStagnation]: max_stagnation 15 -> 100, because stagnation judged on fresh 4-case batches is noise; species_elitism 2.
- Net effect: about 3 weight, 1 bias and 1 delay perturbation per child, instead of about 51, 2 and 25.

Species-count controller in train(), replacing the fixed threshold:
- Start compatibility_threshold = 1.5.
- At the end of each score(), multiply cfg.species_set_config.compatibility_threshold by 1.15 if there are more than 4 species and by 0.87 if fewer than 4. Clamp to 0.3-4.0 and log it in history. DefaultSpeciesSet.speciate re-reads the value every generation.
- Result: about 4 species of about 10 genomes, so 4 elites and 36 new genomes per generation. v2 currently has 10 species, 20 elites and 12 new genomes.
- Dry-run with a dummy fitness first (seconds, no simulation).

Noise handling in train():
- Keep balanced_cases: 4 common-random-number cases per generation, 2 with x-sign +1 and 2 with -1.
- Keep a per-genome record seen[gid] of every case-J, so elites that survive (and are re-evaluated) build up evidence.
- At generations 3, 7, 11 and 15, validate the top 3 genomes by cumulative mean J over at least 8 cases (fallback: batch fitness). Use balanced_cases('validation', 8, 6., offset=500_000): fresh seeds that were not used to select v1 or v2.
- Save the best genome on validation, not the batch champion.
- New flags: --validate-top 3 --validate-every 4.

Calibration knobs in Steer, read from spec['calib'] = {g_theta, g_q, d_bias, twitch}:
- features(): multiply th+/- by g_theta and q+/- by g_q.
- reset(): add d_bias to all hidden-unit biases (self.net.bias[self.net.hidden] += d_bias).
- step(): use twitch ticks instead of TWITCH_TICKS.
- Defaults (1, 1, 0, 3) reproduce the current behaviour.

New stage 'calibrate', with the same budget and the same cases as tune_law:
- Grid: g_theta {0.6, 1, 1.6} x g_q {0.5, 1, 2} x d_bias {+0.1, 0, -0.1, -0.2} x twitch {2, 3, 4} ticks = 108 points.
- This maps one-to-one onto the law grid: k_theta {3, 5, 8}, k_q {0.2, 0.4, 0.8}, threshold {0.4, 0.5, 0.65, 0.8}, width {45, 60, 90} deg.
- Each point is run on balanced_cases('train', 8, 6., offset=900_000), exactly the cases v2's tune_law used: 864 episodes in total.
- Writes calib.json and best_policy_cal.json.

test() changes:
- Accept several --policy name=path entries.
- Report the paired per-case J difference against law_tuned: mean, bootstrap 95% CI, wins out of 16.
- Report per-motor-neuron onset statistics: count, circular mean, resultant length, and % within +-67.5 deg of 135/315 deg. The v2 pass rule is then computed by the script itself.
- Add a validation-split option so diagnostics never use the test seeds.

Run order (new /home/robot/FlapSim-repo/FlapSim/runs/run_steer_v3.sh, outputs in artifacts/spike_steer/v3):
- Start only after tmux session spike_steer_v2 has finished; reuse artifacts/spike_steer/v2/law_tuned.json.
- (a) D1, about 1 min: v1 champion, mirror_spec(v1 champion) and the v2 champion on the v3 validation set. If mirroring does not lower J, the antisymmetry premise is wrong: run v3 without --mirror (2 outputs) but with the template, species-control, noise-handling, calibration and test changes.
- (b) Stage 1, about 62 min: train --mirror --init sparse --balanced --population 40 --cases 4 --generations 16 --seconds 6 --validate-top 3.
- (c) Calibrate, about 20 min: the candidate with the lowest validation J among {v3 champion, mirrored v1, v2 champion}. Optionally a second candidate for +20 min.
- (d) Test, about 4 min, on the shared 16 test cases: pid_retuned, law_strong, law_moderate, law_tuned, snn_cal and snn_raw.
proposals.rationale:
The bottleneck is the search, not capacity or physics:
- The plant is antisymmetric to within about 10%.
- One spiking readout can OR two conjunctions.
- The push-up signal was present in 18 of 20 v1 batches.

Three levers attack the search directly.

(i) Symmetry in the genotype.
- The classical law already hard-codes the same symmetry: it uses psi versus psi+180 deg with one shared threshold. Tying the antagonist pool to the evolved pool is therefore a like-for-like prior, not an unfair advantage.
- It removes the hardest event in the search: building a second coordinated conjunction while keeping the first.
- It halves the genome and makes every case train the same genes (x=+1 cases shape the mirror, x=-1 cases the original).
- Symmetry constraints are an established way to shrink neuroevolution search ([ENSO, Valsalam and Miikkulainen](https://nn.cs.utexas.edu/demos/enso-robots/)).

(ii) Minimal, low-disruption NEAT, which is NEAT's own principle: start minimal and complexify.
- The sparse AND-gate start, with about 3 instead of about 51 perturbations per child, lets selection refine a working circuit instead of re-finding it each generation.
- The species controller keeps about 4 niches. v1 had 1; v2 is running away to 10 or more.
- Fresh validation seeds and accumulated elite evidence reduce the winner's-curse champions seen in v1.

(iii) Separate structure from calibration.
- NEAT is weak at continuous fine-tuning; in this project a NEAT phase-estimating SNN plateaued at about 10 deg error versus 2.4 deg with surrogate gradients.
- The standard remedy is to evolve the topology with NEAT and then tune the weights of the fixed topology with a separate optimizer ([Hybrid Self-Attention NEAT](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2112.03670); CMA-TWEANN, [GECCO 2012](https://unpaywall.org/10.1145%2F2330163.2330288); EANT2, discussed in [DXNN](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1008.2412)).
- Within 2 hours, CMA-ES over all 25-90 weights is out of reach; it needs hundreds of generations.
- Four global knobs mapped one-to-one onto the law's four tuned parameters can be tuned with the law's exact grid, cases and episode count. That makes "same-budget retuned classical law" a literal, auditable equality.

Surrogate gradients are not used:
- There is no differentiable closed loop.
- Imitating the law would only clone it and remove NEAT's role.
- 'Distill the law into the SNN, then evolve' stays as a fallback arm only.

D1 tests the main premise in about 1 minute, and mirrored v1 is a ready fallback if stage 1 under-performs.
proposals.expected_effect:
1. Directions: satisfied by construction. Whatever pool NEAT tunes, its mirror fires half a wingbeat cycle away under the opposite need. Need-up onsets move from about 338 deg (wrong side) to about 150-180 deg, and both sides exceed 20 onsets with at least 70% inside +-67.5 deg.

2. Pitch: on v1's own data, the push-down-capable network already reaches 3.5 deg on x=-1 cases. Mirroring should bring the 8 x=+1 cases from 6.0 deg to about that level. Expected overall pitch RMS is about 3.3-3.6 deg (v1 4.74, law_strong 3.03). This closes the roughly 75% of the J gap that is directional.

3. J:
- Uncalibrated: about 7.0-7.4, because more pulses mean more height error.
- After the 108-point calibration: about 6.2-6.8, that is 0.98-1.08 x the tuned law. On the oracle law grid the same four knobs moved J by up to about 1.5.
- So the 1.05 rule is reachable but not assured. The paired standard error on 16 cases is about 0.3 J, so the decision should use the paired CI.

4. Search behaviour:
- 36 new genomes per generation versus 12 in v2.
- About 3 instead of about 51 weight perturbations per child.
- Fewer crashes at generation 0, because sparse AND gates rarely fire.
- Champions chosen on at least 8 + 8 cases instead of 3-4.
- Flying 16/16 is likely.

5. Interpretation:
- If parity is reached, the claim becomes: NEAT discovers the firing phase, need-gating and delays of an antagonistic motor pair, calibrated with exactly the classical law's tuning budget.
- If not, the remaining gap is the flat J frontier (pitch traded for lift), which no change to the search can remove.

Compute: about 1.5 h total.
- D1: 1 min.
- Stage 1: 2560 six-second episodes plus 96 validation episodes, about 62 min at the measured 43 episodes/min.
- Calibration: 864 episodes, about 20 min.
- Test: about 96 eight-second episodes, about 4 min.
- An optional second calibration adds 0.33 h. Re-tuning the law, if v2's law_tuned.json is missing, adds another 0.33 h.
risks: Exact antisymmetry is a modelling assumption. Pulse authority is antisymmetric to within about 10%, but the need statistics are not: the law's onsets are 87.5% up on x=+1 cases and only 38% up on x=-1 cases. The mirrored network uses symmetric thresholds exactly like the law, so it loses nothing relative to the law, but it cannot exploit the asymmetry an unconstrained network could. D1 checks this before any training.

Scientific framing: 'both directions' becomes a structural prior (an antagonistic pair), not a discovery. v2 (unconstrained) should be reported as the ablation, and only the phase, gating and delays claimed as evolved.

The J frontier is flat: on the oracle law grid, J stays at 6.1-6.8 across very different gain, threshold and width settings. Parity is therefore the realistic ceiling for any search fix. Beating the law needs new information, for example rectified height error and vertical speed as inhibitory inputs; the law would then need the same height gate for a fair comparison.

The sparse AND-gate start is untested in closed loop. If it under-fires, stage 1 stays near the PID (J about 9.7) and the calibration falls back to mirrored v1 or the v2 champion, losing the from-scratch v3 result for this round.
Only one seed fits in 2 hours, and the variance of NEAT outcomes across seeds is unknown. Formal runs need at least 3 seeds, and the 'reliably' claim cannot be made from this pilot.

Calibration and law tuning use the same 8 cases, so both carry the same winner's-curse bias. The 16 fresh test cases are unbiased, but the paired standard error (about 0.3 J) is comparable to the 5% margin.

Changing compatibility_threshold at run time is not an official neat-python API. It works because speciate re-reads the config every generation; confirm with the dummy-fitness dry run before launching.

Separate from v3: the v2 run in progress can still reach 17 species, which raises RuntimeError in _adjust_spawn_exact. With 10 species only 12 genomes per generation are new, so a negative v2 result partly reflects this crippled search, not only the method.

proposals.title: spike_steer v3: mirror-twin motor circuit with direct synapses and a lift-budget pathway
proposals.diagnosis:
I ran no simulations. The figures below were recomputed from artifacts/spike_steer/v1/pilot_test.json, timing_authority.json and timing_law_grid.json. I replayed the gust sign and motor gain of each test seed with pilot.pulse_sign's RNG; this involves no physics.

(1) Why v1 learned one direction (architecture plus data). The single spiking motor neuron could only read 6 dense, randomly wired hidden LIF units. Every 'phase bin AND error sign' conjunction therefore had to be built inside a hidden unit and relayed. Evolution found one of them (push-down: onsets at 338 deg true crank, R=0.90) and never a second. The x-sign of the gust (pulse_sign[0], fixed for each episode) sets which direction is needed, and v1's per-case pitch RMS splits cleanly on it:
- 8 test cases with x-sign -1: v1 3.50 deg (3.12-4.06), law_strong 3.18 deg.
- 8 cases with x-sign +1: v1 5.99 deg (5.46-6.35), law 2.88 deg, PID 7.24 deg.
So v1 is already close to the law in one direction and absent in the other. With 3 random cases per generation, the one-sided solution was often rewarded.

(2) Lift budget: a blind spot shared with the classical law. The 4 test cases with motor gain >= 1.0108 (seeds ...04, 06, 07, 10) need a hover command only 16-29 rad/s above LOW. Their height integrator is already saturated (ki*0.5 = 80*0.5 = 40 rad/s), so the lift a pulse adds cannot be cancelled. Height RMSE in those cases: PID 10.1-18.2 cm, law 14.7-38.0 cm, v1 16.1-30.9 cm. These 4 cases carry 91% of the law's height penalty and 90% of v1's. In the other 12 cases the law costs 6.8 cm against the PID's 6.5 cm. J by stratum (normal / high-gain):

| Controller | Normal | High-gain |
|---|---|---|
| PID | 9.27 | 11.15 |
| law_strong | 5.04 | 10.04 |
| v1 | 7.04 | 11.54 |

In the high-gain stratum v1 is worse than the PID. Just switching between the two existing hand laws by stratum would give J 6.11 instead of 6.29. Neither controller has an input that reveals this budget.

(3) Output design. Each spike triggers a fixed 3-tick twitch with no refractory period. Nothing prevents chained twitches inside one wingbeat, and the longest pulse (6 ms) is shorter than the widest window in the law grid (90 deg, about 5 ticks).

What v2 may still miss:
- Two independent motor neurons double the weights NEAT must tune, which is its known weak point.
- It has no budget input, so even a perfect v2 tops out at about the law's J.
- There is still no refractory period.
- With compatibility 0.6 it already has 6-9 species in a population of 32. With elitism 2 per species, 12-18 of the 32 slots are elites, so selection pressure is weak.
- At generation 3 its validation J (8.59) matches v1 at the same point (8.58).
changes: Put v3 in a NEW module, /home/robot/FlapSim-repo/FlapSim/experiments/algorithms/spike_steer/pilot_v3.py, that imports pilot.py (SpikingGraph, run, SPLITS, CLASSICAL, pulse_sign). Do not edit pilot.py while the v2 tmux chain may still call its tune_law and test stages.

Mirror twin (equivariant under the pitch flip, Z2): when spec['arch']=='twin', Steer.reset builds two SpikingGraph instances from the same spec, with OUTPUTS=1 per copy. That gives 2 motor neurons sharing one genome. Copy A receives x = features(phase, th, q, budget). Copy B receives mirror(x): y[:8] = np.roll(x[:8], 4) (phase + 180 deg); y[8:12] = x[[9, 8, 11, 10]] (th -> -th, q -> -q); the budget part is unchanged. Set self.fired = np.array([fA, fB]), and make run() log which = steer.channel. v1 and v2 specs (inputs=12, no arch) still run on the old path.

Direct synapses, so the classical law becomes a one-neuron special case. Add class SteerGenome(DelayGenome) whose mutate_add_connection allows input -> output edges (sources = inputs + hidden for every target; outputs are never sources), and use it in make_config. initialize(): HIDDEN=4; input->hidden weights N(0, .6); hidden->motor N(0, .5); NEW input->motor edges for all 14 inputs at N(0, .5); delays U{0..8}. Genome 0 keeps every readout weight at 0, including the direct ones, so it equals PID only.

Lift-budget inputs, shared by both copies and not mirrored. INPUTS = 8 phase + 4 need + 2 budget = 14. deficit = clip((40 - (env.teacher.raw[2] - LOW[2]))/40, 0, 3): an efference copy of the unclipped PID motor command. It is 0 with >= 40 rad/s of headroom, about 0.3-0.6 at hover in high-gain cases, and above 1 once the height loop asks for less than LOW. z_up = max(env.last_reading[9], 0)/0.05. Both come from the controller or from the 11-D observation, so the interface is unchanged. Leave the accelerometer out.

Muscle model in Steer.step: TWITCH_TICKS=3. Each further spike from the same channel during a twitch extends it by 1 tick, up to TWITCH_MAX=5 (about 90 deg at 25 Hz, the widest law window); this gives a spike-count to pulse-width code. Add a shared REFRACTORY_TICKS=14 (28 ms) counted from onset, so there is at most one twitch per wingbeat and the two opposite channels cannot both fire in the same wingbeat.

Keep unchanged: the WingbeatPhase PLL (phase and the notched rate estimator.slow), the one-hot 8 x 45 deg phase cells, PITCH_SCALE=.1, RATE_SCALE=1., tau_m=5 ms, tau_s=2.5 ms, spike_scale=5, and evolvable delays of 0-20 ms (1 ms is about 9 deg of fine phase on top of the 45 deg cells).

Batches: pulse_sign() also returns gain = 1 + U(-.015, .015), which is the draw it already replays. Add stratified_cases(): each 4-case batch covers the 4 (x, y) sign combinations, with exactly one case (rotating each generation) of gain >= 1.008. Validation: 8 cases (sign combinations x 2) including 2 high-gain cases. tune_law uses the same sampler. Before launching, do a dry run that checks the sampled signs and gains (RNG only, no physics).

NEAT run: python -m experiments.algorithms.spike_steer.pilot_v3 train --arch twin --batch stratified --population 32 --generations 16 --cases 4 --seconds 6 --compatibility 1.5 --validate-every 4 --seed 1 --output runs/spike_steer/pilot_v3_s1. The compatibility of 1.5 aims for 2-4 species. Selection by validation J is unchanged.

Fair classical comparator with the same information: the law fires only when |u| > u0 + k_h*deficit and the PLL phase is inside the window centred at psi (need up) or psi + 180 deg. Grid around v2's best (k_theta, k_q): u0 in {.4, .5, .65, .8} x w in {60, 90} deg x k_h in {0, .5, 1.5} x psi in {135, 158} deg = 48 laws x 8 stratified training cases of 6 s (384 episodes). The best law with k_h=0 becomes law_tuned_v3; the best overall becomes law_gate_tuned.

Test on the same 16 test cases (cases('test', 16, 8.)): pid_retuned, law_tuned (v2's grid), law_tuned_v3, law_gate_tuned, snn_v2, snn_v3, plus three test-time lesions of snn_v3. Lesions: no_budget (budget inputs forced to 0), one_copy (copy B silenced), fixed_twitch (no extension). That is 9 x 16 = 144 episodes; reuse the PID, v1 and law_strong numbers from artifacts/spike_steer/v1/pilot_test.json. Report results overall and by stratum (gain >= 1.008 vs below), paired wins, onset-phase histograms by channel x need sign with resultant length, onsets per second by stratum, and the deficit at each onset.

Unit test, tests/test_spike_steer.py: for a random twin spec, copy B's input at (phi, th, q) equals copy A's input at (phi + pi, -th, -q), and the two copies emit identical spike trains when given the mirrored input sequences.

v3 pass criteria. (a) 16/16 flown. (b) J_snn <= 1.05 x J_law_gate_tuned, J_snn < J_law_tuned, and at least 11/16 paired wins against law_tuned. (c) At least 20 onsets for each need sign; at least 70% of each channel's onsets within +-67.5 deg of that channel's mean phase; the two channel means 180 +- 30 deg apart. (d) The no_budget lesion raises height RMSE in the high-gain stratum by at least 3 cm.
proposals.rationale:
Each change targets a measured cause, and the comparison with the classical law stays fair.

(a) Symmetry. In timing_authority.json the pitch-rate effect of a pulse is antisymmetric under psi -> psi+180 deg: |pr(psi) + pr(psi+180)| <= 0.24 rad/s against effects of 1.6-2.7 rad/s, a mismatch of about 6-9%. The classical law already assumes this symmetry. Tying the two motor neurons through shared weights halves what NEAT has to tune, which matters because fine-tuning weights is its documented weakness. It also makes "one direction only" structurally impossible. The firing phase is still discovered; only the 180 deg relation is imposed, and that relation is physics.

(b) Direct input-to-motor synapses put the law inside what a single LIF neuron can represent: bias, one phase cell, positive need weights and a negative weight on the opposing rate together reproduce |u| > u0 inside the window. With tau 5/2.5 ms, a one-hot phase input reaches only about 40% of its steady-state PSP within its 5 ms bin. The motor neuron therefore acts as a coincidence detector between a phasic phase input and a tonic need drive, like an insect steering motor neuron. The hidden units only have to add refinements, not rebuild the conjunctions.

(c) The lift budget is the largest remaining lever, and it is information the law lacks. The PID's saturating integrator and the LOW clip already integrate height over seconds, so the efference copy gives the network a slow state without slow neurons or adaptation currents.

(d) The refractory period and graded twitch match the law's structure (one window per wingbeat, 60-90 deg wide) and add a spike-count code. A test-time lesion measures what the graded twitch contributes.

(e) Keep the PLL. Its adaptive notch is indispensable: the 4.41 deg rocking at 24.9 Hz puts about 12 rad/s on the gyro, against a law rate threshold of 1.25 rad/s. NEAT phase estimators already failed in this project (9.3 deg against 6.9 deg for the PLL). Timing tolerance (about +-45 deg) is far larger than the PLL error. Using the identical PLL for the law and the network isolates the controller. A clock-spike encoding (spikes at PLL phase 0 and 180 deg, with timing set by evolved delays) is a sensible later ablation.

(f) Leave the accelerometer out. The gust torque already appears in the notched gyro within 1-2 ticks. accel_x is dominated by wingbeat vibration and would need its own notch of unknown quality, and each extra input adds 4-5 random weights for NEAT to tune.

(g) Fairness. The law receives the same deficit signal and is tuned on the same stratified cases, including its phase. The no_budget, one_copy and fixed_twitch lesions separate what the architecture contributes from what the extra information contributes.
proposals.expected_effect:
Both directions are covered by construction. v1's push-down quality (3.50 deg pitch RMS in the x-sign -1 cases) should carry over to the x-sign +1 cases, where v1 had 5.99 deg. Overall pitch RMS is then about 3.3-3.7 deg (v1 4.74, law_strong 3.03).

In the high-gain stratum, height should drop from about 23-25 cm to about 14-18 cm, at a cost of roughly 1 deg of pitch. That gives J_hi of about 9.0-9.6 (law_strong 10.04, v1 11.54, PID 11.15).

Overall J_v3 should be about 6.0-6.5 (v1 8.17, law_strong 6.29, PID 9.74). This should pass the v2 criterion (J <= 1.05 x the tuned law) and beat law_tuned by about 0.2-0.4. Most of that margin should come from the high-gain stratum and should disappear under the no_budget lesion.

Against law_gate_tuned, which has the same information, the realistic outcome is parity (within +-5%), not a clear win. The honest claim is: law-level performance, with phase, direction coupling and lift budgeting discovered by evolution rather than hand-designed, plus a neural mechanism visible in the lesions.

Expected lesion results:
- one_copy should reproduce v1's one-sided pattern (about 6 deg pitch in x-sign +1 cases).
- If fixed_twitch costs more than 0.2 J, a proportional-width law must be added before claiming any advantage from the spike-count code.
risks: Information versus architecture: most of any gain over law_tuned will come from the deficit input, and law_gate_tuned will probably match the network. Report parity plus autonomous discovery, not superiority, unless J_snn < J_law_gate_tuned in at least 11 of 16 paired cases.

The high-gain stratum is small: only 4 test cases have gain >= 1.0108 and 6 have gain >= 1.008, so per-stratum claims are noisy. If the result is borderline, add a second 16-case test set (about 6 more minutes).

The imposed symmetry is only approximate (pulse authority asymmetric by up to about 9%, plus PID trim). If it caps performance, add a channel-identity input (+1 for copy A, -1 for copy B) with zero initial weights.

NEAT may not find the inhibitory budget weights in 16 generations, since fine-tuning weights is its weak point. Check the champion's direct deficit-to-motor weight at generation 8. If it is not negative, the fallback is a declared prior: initialise that weight with mean -0.5.
The graded twitch can add lift and confounds the comparison with fixed-window laws. The fixed_twitch lesion measures this, and a proportional-width law is needed if it matters.
Several changes land at once. The direct synapses and the refractory period are not lesioned separately, so attribution is limited to the budget, the twin and the twitch.
Reviewers may see the efference copy of the PID motor command as privileged. It is computed from the rangefinder height that is already in the observation. Fallback: use only z_up and vz_up.
Operational: v2's chain may still call pilot.py. Keep v3 in pilot_v3.py and start it only after v2's test stage finishes, because all 18 cores are busy.
If the stratified sampler replays the RNG wrongly, the batch composition changes silently. Assert the signs and gains of the sampled seeds in a dry run that uses only the RNG, with no physics.

proposals.title: Height-budgeted objective with motor-gain-stratified, PID-paired, information-matched selection and testing (spike_steer pilot v3)
proposals.diagnosis:
Conclusion: v1 trails the classical law for two separate reasons, and v2 fixes only the first. The second one sits in the objective and the evaluation, not in the network.

(1) The SNN learned one direction. On the 16 test cases its pitch RMS is 3.1-4.1 deg in exactly the 8 cases with x-force sign -1, and 5.5-6.4 deg in all 8 with +1. The x-force sign is pulse_sign[0]; the 6 mN x-force on the lower body sets the pitch-disturbance direction, and the 8 uN.m y-torque is minor. So the network is a single 'push-down' circuit. It never grew an up-pathway, even after three all-'+' batches (gens 5, 8, 10). This is a search/exposure problem, and v2's (sx, sy)-balanced batches and 2 motor neurons target it.

(2) The height cost depends on a variable the network cannot see: motor_gain. For g above about 1.009, the hover command (3178/g) has to sit more than 40 rad/s below p['motor'] = 3190. The clipped height integrator (ki 80 x 0.5 = 40 rad/s) cannot supply that, so the PID already hovers near LOW with a standing offset and cannot shed pulse lift.
- On the v1 test, seeds ..04/06/07/10 (g = 1.011-1.015) give law_strong +4.6 to +19.8 cm and the SNN +6.0 to +18.6 cm of height RMSE over the PID.
- Every case with g < 1.005 stays within +0.6 cm.
- So pulses are almost free in about 75% of cases and very expensive in the rest. The SNN sees only phase, pitch and rate, so like the fixed law it can only pick one compromise. It has no structural way to beat the law on the trade-off.

(3) Batch composition, not skill, drives selection.
- v1: 10 of 20 three-case batches had no low-room case.
- The selected policy came from gen 15, the only batch with two low-room cases (fit_max -9.81).
- The pulse-heavy late champion (gen 19: 5.1% duty, 19.6 cm on validation) came after two batches with none.
- v2 still draws motor_gain at random: 7 of 25 batches have no low-room case and 10 of 25 have 2-3, so its fitness will swing the same way.

(4) J = pitch + 0.3 x height is mis-specified.
- It is flat along the aggressive half of the front. On the oracle law grid, settings that fly every case stay at J 6.25-6.43 across 2.3-3.3 deg pitch and 10.1-13.2 cm height. So where the network lands on the front is noise.
- It rewards v3 height failures (height RMSE >= 15 cm): law_strong 3/16, SNN 4/16, PID 1/16.
- It would reject a strictly better trade-off. An oracle 'room' schedule (law_strong when g <= 1.0095, PID otherwise) scores J 6.56 versus law_strong 6.29.
- Re-scored on the v1 rows with the budgeted objective below (post-stratified): room-oracle 6.21, law_moderate 7.77, law_strong 8.33, PID 9.69, SNN v1 11.01. That puts the SNN behind even the PID. The ranking holds for delta in {0.5, 1, 2} cm, barrier in {1, 1.7, 3} deg/cm and v3 penalty in {0, 3}.

(5) The evaluation is weak.
- The test seeds 2_020_100_000-015 are the gates evaluate/stress split. They were already used for the PID retune and for the v1->v2 decisions, so they are spent.
- They hold 6/16 low-room cases where about 4 are expected, which inflates the height error of pulse controllers.
- v1 validated only the 3-case champion, on 8 six-second cases with 1 low-room case (validation 7.57, test 8.17).
- The full-episode height RMSE includes the takeoff, which is the same for every controller.
- The classical law was selected on training data only, and only its J-optimal point was compared.
- No paired CIs, no v3 success rate, and only one training seed.

What v2 may still miss: all of (2)-(5).
- It can pass J <= 1.05 x J_law (margin about 0.31, the size of J's variation along the front and about one SE of a 16-case paired mean) by sitting on the classical front while failing v3 height more often than the PID.
- Its 108-point J-tuned law will be an aggressive point. The grid is also inefficient, because the law depends only on k_theta/threshold and k_q/threshold.
- tune_law stores no per-case rows, so nothing can be re-scored under another objective.
changes: run() in experiments/algorithms/spike_steer/pilot.py: also return height_late_m (RMS of true z from env.samples[:,2] for t >= 2 s, the same window as pitch), slope_late_m_s (polyfit over t >= 2 s), success = m['success'], motor_gain = float(env.motor_gain) and pulse_sign = env.pulse_sign.tolist(). Tag every onset with the current low_room value. When c has 'stratum', assert that env.motor_gain and env.pulse_sign match case_draw(c['seed']).

Add objective_budget(r, ref) with pre-registered constants BUDGET_CM = 1.0, BARRIER = 1.7 deg/cm, CAP_CM = 10, V3_PENALTY = 3. A crash scores 60 - elapsed; otherwise J_b = pitch_rms_deg + 0.3*100*height_late_m + 1.7*clip(100*(height_late_m - ref['height_late_m']) - 1.0, 0, 10) + 3*(not success), where ref is the retuned PID (Steer(None, None)) on the same case and length. Keep the old J (pitch + 0.3 x full-episode height) as 'objective_J' for continuity. Fitness = -(weighted mean of J_b over the batch).

Paired PID references: score() adds a ('pid_ref', c, None, None) task for each batch case to the same executor.map, which costs 4 extra 6 s episodes per generation. The validation, tune_law and test stages compute their references once per case set.

Stratified, importance-weighted cases. Replace pulse_sign() with case_draw(seed) -> (motor_gain, signs), using the same RNG order as HoverEnv.reset. Add stratified_cases(split, per_stratum, seconds, offset): strata are sx = pulse_sign[0] in {+1, -1} crossed with low_room = motor_gain > 1.0075 (natural share 25%). Set c['weight'] = 1.5 for high-room and 0.5 for low-room cases, so weighted means are unbiased for the natural mix. Case counts: training 1 per stratum per generation (4 x 6 s, offset seed*100_000 + gen*1_000); validation 4 per stratum (16 x 8 s); classical tuning 2 per stratum (8 x 6 s, offset 900_000); test 8 per stratum (32 x 8 s, about the variance-optimal allocation given a low-room paired SD of 3-9 against 0.3-1.4 for high-room).

Fresh splits, none used anywhere in the repo: SPLITS.update(train3=2_050_100_000, validation3=2_051_100_000, test3=2_052_100_000). Treat 2_020_100_000-015 (the v1/v2 test, which is also the gates evaluate/stress split) as dev-only from now on.

Information parity: both arms get the same extra signal, computed inside the controller from the existing range-finder height loop. low_room = clip((80 - (env.teacher.raw[2] - LOW[2]))/80, 0, 2), low-passed with tau 50 ms in Steer and reset in Steer.reset. SNN: INPUTS = N_PHASE + 5 (13th input); features() returns x[:self.net.n_inputs] so the 12-input v1/v2 specs still run; a spec key 'clamp_inputs': [12] gives the ablation. Classical law: fire iff |u| > threshold*(1 + k_room*low_room); k_room = 0 reproduces the old law. If another lens changes the SNN inputs, the classical arm must get the same information.

tune_law, parametrized without the scale redundancy (the law is invariant to a common scale of k_theta, k_q and threshold): threshold = 1, k_theta = G with G in {5, 7, 10, 14, 20}, k_q = r*G with r fixed at the k_q/k_theta of v2's tuned law, width in {60, 90} deg, k_room in {0, 1, 3}, psi_off in {-20, 0, +20} deg added to PULSE_PHASE. The SNN effectively tunes its own firing phase, so the law must be allowed to as well. That is 90 points x 8 stratified train3 cases = 720 six-second episodes. Save every per-case row; v2 stores only means. If the winner lies on a grid edge, extend one step in that direction.

SNN training: --init-from runs/spike_steer/pilot_v2_s1/best_policy.json, used only if v2 met its two-direction criterion. Genome 0 is v2's best plus zero-weight edges from input -13 to every hidden node; genomes 1-31 are copies with weight noise N(0, 0.3) and new-input weights N(0, 0.6). Run 12 generations x 32 genomes x 4 cases. If v2 failed the direction criterion, use a fresh initialize() and 15 generations. Keep v2's neat.ini unchanged (compatibility 0.6, 2 outputs) and keep the objective fixed for the whole run (no weight annealing), so objective, selection and information are the only differences.

Symmetric validation-based selection. SNN: at generations 2, 5, 8 and 11, validate the top-2 genomes by current fitness (from distinct species when available) on the 16 validation3 cases at 8 s, giving 8 candidates. Classical: take the top-6 grid points plus the top-2 with k_room = 0, ranked by training J_b, on the same 16 cases, also 8 candidates. Both arms pick the argmin of weighted validation J_b (snn_v3, law_Jb, law_noroom). Write all candidate rows and report the validation-minus-test optimism.

Classical trade-off front: from the tuning rows, take the non-dominated set in (weighted pitch_late, weighted height excess over the PID) and keep the points nearest to 0, 2 and 5 cm excess (law_front_0, law_front_2, law_front_5) for the test.

Run the test once, on 32 stratified test3 cases of 8 s, with 10 controllers (320 episodes): pid_retuned, law_v2 (v2's tune_law best), law_Jb, law_noroom, law_front_0/2/5, snn_v2, snn_v3 and snn_v3_noroom (13th input clamped to 0). Report: flown and v3 success counts with Wilson 95% intervals; post-stratified means (stratum weights 0.375/0.375/0.125/0.125); stratified paired-bootstrap 95% CIs (10 000 replicates, reusing wingbeat_snn/paper_stats.bootstrap within strata) for dJ_b, dpitch, height excess and old dJ; the matched-excess dpitch of each SNN against the classical test front (lower hull of the PID and the 5 laws, rebuilt in every replicate); a per-stratum table; onset-phase histograms by need direction; onset rate by low_room.

Pre-register before the test stage by writing it into results.json: the constants above and the decision rule. 'Better trade-off' requires all four: snn_v3 flies 32/32; its v3 successes are >= law_Jb's; the upper CI bound of post-stratified dJ_b(snn_v3 - law_Jb) is < 0; and the upper CI bound of matched-excess dpitch is < 0. 'Matches' means the upper CI bound of dJ_b is < +0.5. Anything else is a negative result. Learning versus information is judged by comparing (snn_v3 - snn_v3_noroom) with (law_Jb - law_noroom). Run in tmux only after v2 finishes.
proposals.rationale:
(a) 'Better trade-off' becomes one well-posed number: pitch at a per-case height budget relative to the same PID, with the v3 success criterion built in.
- In high-room cases the barrier never binds (all laws stay within +0.6 cm), so J_b rewards the most pitch reduction per pulse, which is the quality of timing and need-gating.
- In low-room cases the barrier dominates, so J_b rewards withholding lift.
- A fixed law cannot do both. That gap, about 1.6 points on the v1 rows, is exactly what a learned, state-dependent gate could exploit, and moving along the front no longer pays.
- Because the barrier is relative to the same-case PID, cases where the PID itself flies high are not punished. The old J is still reported.

(b) Stratification and paired PID references take the dominant nuisance variable (motor_gain) out of fitness and selection. Importance weights keep every estimate unbiased for the natural case mix, and the 50/50 room split at test narrows the heavy-tailed low-room CIs.

(c) Information parity plus the 2x2 ablation (learner x room input) makes any gain attributable, either to learning or to the new information. Without this, an SNN gain could simply be the information effect.

(d) Both arms get the same objective, the same training distribution, the same validation set, the same number of validated candidates and 8 s selection episodes. One fresh test, a pre-registered rule and a matched-height front comparison that depends on no weight make the verdict trustworthy whichever way it falls. The front comparison also guards against a different choice of weight being used to argue a win.

(e) The classical law is tuned over the dimensions the SNN effectively tunes (gain/ratio, window, phase offset, room schedule), parametrized without the k_theta/k_q/threshold redundancy of the v2 grid.

(f) The warm start reuses v2's direction learning, so the 2-hour go/no-go tests the new trade-off pressure rather than re-learning phase locking.
proposals.expected_effect:
Training: the batch-driven swings between pulse-heavy and pulse-light champions should disappear, and the gap between validation and test (v1: +0.6) should shrink.

Expected J_b of the baselines, from the v1 rows:
- best fixed law: about 7.8
- room-scheduled law: about 6.2-6.8 (oracle split 6.21)
- PID: about 9.7
- v2's J-tuned law and snn_v2: probably 8 or worse (J-trained, no room input)

snn_v3: both directions (from v2) plus room gating should bring it to about 6.5-7.5. To beat law_Jb it has to gain in the high-room stratum through timing or anticipation. That is where the paired SD is small (about 0.3-1.4), so a 16-case stratum CI is about +-0.2-0.6. The overall post-stratified CI with 32 cases is about +-0.5-0.8.

The run ends in one of three pre-registered verdicts: better trade-off, matches, or negative. The 2x2 ablation then says whether any gain comes from learning or from information. A negative verdict is a clean negative result and the signal to change topic.

Compute: about 97 min at the stated 24 episodes/min for 8 s episodes (refs 2.4, SNN training 48, SNN validation 5.3, classical grid 22.5, classical validation 5.3, test 13.3), about 1.3 h at v2's observed throughput, and at most about 1.9 h if training from scratch for 15 generations plus one grid extension.
risks: The objective is being changed after seeing the v1/v2 results, which is an analyst degree of freedom. Mitigation: pre-register J_b and the decision rule, justify J_b by the existing v3 success criterion, cite the robustness sweep (ranking unchanged for delta 0.5-2 cm, barrier 1-3 deg/cm, penalty 0-3), and still report the old J and the full front.
The room-scheduled classical law may capture all the value of the new signal, so the SNN at best ties. That is the likely outcome, and it is still a clean, reportable answer.

12 warm-start generations may be too few for NEAT (weight mutation power 0.2) to grow room-gating weights from zero; starting from scratch is riskier still. With one seed there is no method-level claim; the RUNBOOK sign test needs at least 6 seeds.

The barrier makes both arms conservative in low-room cases, which shrinks the differences. That stratum is also heavy-tailed (paired SD 3-9), so the overall CIs may still straddle 0. The high-room stratum is the lower-noise comparison.

Budget asymmetry: the SNN gets 1536 episodes plus 3200 inherited from v2, the classical law 720 plus 1728 inherited. Mitigation: show the classical tuning has saturated (interior optimum, validated top-8 within 1 SE) and extend the grid if the winner is on an edge.
Predicting the strata relies on HoverEnv.reset drawing from its RNG in the current order. The assert in run() catches any change.

Stratifying and weighting by a hidden case parameter can look like tailoring. It is used only for sampling and weights; neither controller ever sees motor_gain. Also report the unweighted per-stratum results.
6 s training against 8 s selection/test, and late-window against the official full-episode height RMSE, can disagree. Selection is done at 8 s, and both height metrics are reported.

low_room comes from the PID height loop, which inherits the range-finder's 20 ms delay and observer noise. It is low-passed at 50 ms. Any input change proposed by another lens must also be given to the classical arm.
With the 0.5 importance weight, height discipline may be too weak a training signal. Fallback, declared in advance: unweighted 50/50 training, keeping weighted validation and test.

ranking.title: v3 search fix: mirror-tied antagonist-pair NEAT with a sparse start and gentle mutation, then a 4-knob calibration with the same budget as the classical law
ranking.reason:
Best fit to the v2 criteria, and its search diagnosis checks out against the code and neat-python 2.0.0.
- v1 history shows 1 species for all 20 generations.
- DelayConnectionGene defaults: the delay mutation power falls back to 3 ms, and delay_replace_rate 0.03 resets about 2.5 delays per child to the implicit initial value of 0 ms. With rate 0.6 x 82 genes, each child perturbs about 50 weights and about 25 delays.
- v2 is at 10 species. Elitism applies per species, so most of each generation is unchanged elites. _adjust_spawn_exact raises RuntimeError at 17 or more species, because the effective min_species_size is max(2, elitism) = 2 and 17 x 2 > 32.
- Mirror tying is justified by timing_authority.json: with 90 deg windows, +2.70 / -2.46 rad/s at 135 / 315 deg and +2.74 / -2.52 at 180 / 0 deg. A replay of v1's batch RNG shows 18 of 20 batches had an sx=+1 case, so the search failed while the training signal was there.
- The 1-minute D1 premise check, mirrored v1 as a fallback, and calibration on the law's own 8 tuning cases are the right ideas.

Weaknesses:
- Its proposed validation set (offset 500k) has 5 of 8 cases with motor gain >= 1.008 (replayed RNG). The law-tuning set has 3 of 8 and the test 6 of 16, so selection would be biased toward under-firing.
- It ignores motor-gain stratification, which is the main J driver. In the 6 high-gain test cases law_strong's height RMSE is 18.1 cm vs the PID's 10.6; elsewhere it is 6.5 vs 6.4.
- The sparse AND-gate restart is untested and could spend the hour near PID performance.
- Shifting the hidden biases would silence v1's spontaneously active unit (bias 1.02).
- '75% of the gap is directional' is optimistic. Within low-gain cases the sx=-1 gap is still 0.6 J, so about 0.8 of the 1.9 J gap remains after mirroring. A realistic calibrated J is 6.6-7.1, not 6.2-6.8.

ranking.title: spike_steer v3: mirror-twin motor circuit with direct synapses and a lift-budget pathway
ranking.reason:
Its core change is the same mirror (the twin is equivalent to mirror_spec, but needs two Graph instances and a new Steer path). It has a good equivalence unit test, a correct gain-stratified batch design, and useful lesions.

Its lift-budget diagnosis is verified: the 4 test cases with gain >= 1.0108 carry 91% of law_strong's height excess over the PID. A spike triggers a fixed 3-tick twitch with no refractory period.

Problems:
- It bundles new information (the deficit input) with architecture changes. Any gain over the v2 law would come from information, not learning, and against its own fair comparator (law_gate_tuned) the expected result is parity.
- The measured lever is small. law_strong and law_moderate tie at J of about 8.55 in high-gain cases, and switching laws by stratum gains only about 0.03-0.18 J.
- It adds 14 inputs plus direct synapses for NEAT, which is weak at weight tuning, without fixing the disruptive mutation, the delay defaults or the species explosion.
- A shared 28 ms refractory period would cut v1's chained twitches (its onsets spread from 270 to 45 deg).
- Its pass rules are stricter than v2's.

Worth keeping: the twin unit test, the stratified sampler, the lesions, and the deficit-input arm for a later information-parity study.

ranking.title: Height-budgeted objective with motor-gain-stratified, PID-paired, information-matched selection and testing (spike_steer pilot v3)
ranking.reason:
The strongest critique of the evaluation, and it is verified (RNG replay, no physics):
- The test seeds 2_020_100_000+ are the gates 'evaluate' stress split, already used for earlier decisions.
- 6 of 16 test cases have gain > 1.0075, against about 4 expected.
- The v1 and v2 validation sets each have only 1 of 8 high-gain cases, which explains v1's validation-to-test optimism (7.57 -> 8.17).
- v1 batches had no low-room case in 10 of 20 generations and were all sx=+1 in generations 5, 8 and 10.
- tune_law saves no per-case rows.

As a plan for passing v2, though:
- It replaces J with J_b, so it optimizes something other than the criterion being judged.
- It has no structural fix for the one-direction failure; it relies on v2 having learned it, or on a fresh initialization.
- It spends the budget on a 32-case, 10-controller test and on importance weighting.

Adopt now: the fresh test split, per-case rows, stratification and pre-registration. Keep J_b and the 2x2 information-parity ablation for the formal phase.

changes:
Put v3 in a new module, experiments/algorithms/spike_steer/pilot_v3.py, that imports pilot.py (SpikingGraph, Steer, run, cases, balanced_cases, SPLITS).
- Do not edit pilot.py or the v2 script, and launch nothing until tmux session spike_steer_v2 has logged 'test exit'.
- Reuse artifacts/spike_steer/v2/law_tuned.json and the v1/v2 test rows (PID, law_strong, law_moderate, law_tuned, v2 champion) on the old 16-case test. Their reproduction is also a free determinism check.

Mirror-tied antagonist pool (from P1/P2):
- Add MIRROR = (4,5,6,7,0,1,2,3,9,8,11,10): phase cell +180 deg, th+ <-> th-, q+ <-> q-.
- mirror_spec(spec) appends a copy of every node (id + 100000) and every edge (input source -(i+1) becomes -(MIRROR[i]+1)) and adds the mirrored motor neuron to 'outputs'.
- export() returns mirror_spec(...) under --tied. The NEAT genome keeps num_outputs = 1.
- SpikingGraph, Steer and run() work unchanged (which = 0 original, 1 mirror).
- Unit test: copy B's spike train under mirrored inputs equals copy A's under the original inputs.

Opposite-direction lockout in Steer:
- An onset from one motor pool blocks onsets from the other pool for 14 ticks (28 ms). This is reciprocal inhibition between antagonists, and it stops the two pools firing in the same wingbeat when pitch and rate have opposite signs.
- Same-direction chaining stays allowed, because v1 relies on chained twitches.
- Adopt it only if D1 shows it does not raise J.

Gain- and sign-stratified case sampling (from P2/P3):
- case_draw(seed) returns (motor_gain, signs) by replaying HoverEnv.reset's RNG.
- stratified_cases() gives every 4-case block all four (sx, sy) combinations, with exactly one case of gain >= 1.008 in a rotating slot (about the natural 23-25%).
- An RNG-only dry run asserts the signs and gains before launch.
- Fresh splits: training 'train' offset 300000 + gen*1000; NEAT validation 'validation' offset 600000 (8 cases); D1 offset 700000 (16); final selection offset 800000 (16).

Warm start instead of P1's untested sparse restart:
- Build DelayGenome objects from the D1-chosen spec (default: the v1 champion): biases, weights, delays and enabled flags. Innovation numbers come from tracker.get_innovation_number(src, dst, 'shared_initial'); node_indexer starts at 32.
- Add 4 zero-weight direct edges from th+/th-/q+/q- to the motor neuron, so NEAT can add direct need excitation or inhibition. The law fires in the correct direction 97% of the time with the same inputs; v1 does 85%.
- Genome 0 is the exact source, so mirror(v1) stays in the population. Genomes 1-31 are the source after two rounds of the v3 template's mutate().

Gentle template neat_template_v3.ini (P1, adapted to the roughly 86-gene warm start):
- Weights: weight_mutate_rate 0.1, power 0.15, replace 0.01.
- Biases: bias_mutate_rate 0.2, power 0.05, replace 0.
- Delays: delay_mutate_rate 0.05, delay_mutate_power 1.0, delay_replace_rate 0, delay_init_mean 4, delay_init_stdev 2. These are currently the implicit 3 ms and 0 +- 0.
- Structure: node_add_prob 0.05 (a spiking relay with bias 0 is not neutral), node_delete_prob 0.02, conn_add 0.2, conn_delete 0.05.
- Reproduction: elitism 1, survival_threshold 0.25, min_species_size 2.
- Stagnation: max_stagnation 100, species_elitism 2.

Species-count controller (from P1):
- Start compatibility_threshold at the median pairwise genome distance of generation 0, measured in a dummy-fitness dry run that takes seconds.
- After each score(), multiply cfg.species_set_config.compatibility_threshold by 1.15 if there are more than 4 species, or by 0.87 if fewer than 3. Clamp to 0.1-4.0 and log it. speciate() re-reads the value every generation.
- This keeps about 3-4 species, far from the 17-species RuntimeError.

Selection (from P1/P3):
- Every 4 generations, validate the top 3 genomes on the 8 NEAT-validation cases (6 s).
- After training, run the 3 best validated genomes plus the D1 winner on the 16 final-selection cases.
- Pick the lowest J among candidates that fly 16/16 and meet the onset rule on those cases. Write the choice to results.json before calibration and test.

Calibration knobs (P1, modified). Steer reads spec['calib'] = {g_theta, g_q, d_out, twitch}:
- th+/- is multiplied by g_theta and q+/- by g_q.
- d_out is added to the motor-neuron biases of both pools. This is a clean threshold knob that leaves the hidden phase detectors intact.
- twitch sets the twitch length in ticks.
- The defaults (1, 1, 0, 3) must reproduce the current spikes (unit test).
- Grid: g_theta {0.6, 1, 1.6} x g_q {0.5, 1, 2} x d_out {-0.3, -0.15, 0, +0.15} x twitch {2, 3, 4} = 108 points, the same count as the law grid.
- Run on exactly the law's tuning cases, balanced_cases('train', 8, 6., offset=900000): 864 episodes.
- Rank by flying all cases first, then by mean J. Save per-case rows.

Secondary fairness comparator, law_ext (from P3):
- 72 points around v2's best law, adding a phase offset. Its onsets average 163 deg (up) and 342 deg (down) in true crank phase, so its phase was never tuned.
- Grid: psi_off {-30, -15, 0, +15} deg x threshold scale {0.8, 1, 1.25} x width {45, 60, 90} deg x k_q scale {0.5, 1}.
- Same 8 cases (576 episodes), per-case rows saved.
- Reported next to law_tuned, but not part of the v2 pass rule.

Test (from P1/P3). The script computes the v2 rule itself from the onset rows, not from the 45 deg histograms:
- flown count;
- J ratio against law_tuned;
- for each need class (true need from the oracle): at least 20 onsets, and the share within +-67.5 deg of 135 / 315 deg in true crank phase.

It also reports the paired bootstrap 95% CI of dJ, wins out of 16, and tables by gain stratum (>= 1.008) and by sx.

Old 16-case test: new runs only for snn_v3 (calibrated), snn_v3_raw, mirror_v1 and law_ext (64 episodes of 8 s).

Fresh 16-case test: consecutive seeds from test3 = 2_052_100_000, 8 s, all 9 controllers (144 episodes): pid_retuned, law_strong, law_moderate, law_tuned, law_ext, snn_v3, snn_v3_raw, mirror_v1, v2 champion.
v3_plan.run_config:
Start only after tmux session spike_steer_v2 logs 'test exit' (about 02:40). Run in one tmux session: tmux new-session -d -s spike_steer_v3 "bash runs/run_steer_v3.sh 2>&1 | tee -a runs/spike_steer_v3.log". Use PYTHON=/home/robot/miniconda3/envs/mujoco/bin/python, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 and 18 workers. Outputs go to runs/spike_steer/pilot_v3_s3 and are copied to artifacts/spike_steer/v3.

0. selftest (seconds): mirror-equivalence and knob-default unit tests, RNG-only dry run of the stratified samplers, dummy-fitness species dry run.
1. D1, about 3 min: 16 fresh stratified validation cases (4 high-gain) x 6 s, 96 episodes. Controllers: pid_retuned, law_tuned (v2), v1, mirror(v1), mirror(v1)+lockout, v2 champion.
2. train, about 55 min, 2048 + 96 episodes: --tied --warm-start <D1 winner> --template neat_template_v3.ini --population 32 --cases 4 --batch stratified --generations 16 --seconds 6 --species-target 3-4 --validate-top 3 --validate-every 4 --validation-cases 8 --seed 3.
3. select, about 2 min, 64 episodes: the 3 best validated genomes plus the D1 winner on the 16 final-selection cases.
4. calibrate, about 21 min: 108 points x the law's 8 tuning cases (864 episodes).
5. tune_law_ext, about 14 min: 72 points x the same 8 cases (576 episodes).
6. test, about 7 min: old 16-case test (64 new episodes) plus fresh 16-case test (144 episodes), 8 s each.

Total is about 1.7 h at v2's measured 41.7 six-second episodes per minute, and about 2.1 h at the conservative 24 eight-second episodes per minute.

Optional fallback: if the selected candidate's best calibrated tuning-case J exceeds 1.10 x law_tuned's tuning-case J, also calibrate the runner-up and keep the lower tuning-case J. This adds 0.35 h and must be disclosed as 216 vs 108 calibration points. Run it only if the measured total stays at or below 2.5 h.

Wait for each stage with a background completion notice, not sleep polling.
v3_plan.if_v2_failed_how:
First compute the v2 rule from the rows in artifacts/spike_steer/v2/test.json (not the 45 deg histograms): flown count, J ratio, onset count and in-window share for each need class, plus tables by gain (>= 1.008) and by sx. If v2's training crashed with RuntimeError (17 or more species), use its last best_policy.json and classify the result the same way. Then branch.

(A) Directions failed. This is likely: v1 had 0% of need-up onsets in the 135 deg window.
- Run the plan as written: mirror tying is the core change, the lockout follows D1, and the warm start is mirror(v1).
- If D1 shows mirror(v1) does not beat v1 by at least 0.3 J, or its need-up in-window share is below 70%, the antisymmetry premise fails. Drop --tied and warm-start an untied 2-output network from v2's champion, or from v1 with output 1 initialised as v1's mirror but untied. Keep the stratified batches, the template, species control and calibration.

(B) Directions passed but J > 1.05 x law.
- Do not mirror unless D1 shows mirror(v1) beats v2's champion; warm-start the untied v2 champion.
- If most of the gap is height in gain >= 1.008 cases (over-firing), the levers are d_out, twitch and the lockout.
- If most of the gap is pitch in gain < 1.008 cases (timing or gating), the levers are the direct need->motor edges and the NEAT refinement.
- If the paired CI straddles the 5% margin, rely on the fresh 16-case test rather than changing the method.
- Do not add a lift-budget input in v3. The measured lever is 0.03-0.18 J, and fairness would require giving it to the law too; it belongs to a v4 information-parity arm with a law_gate_tuned comparator.

(C) Fewer than 16/16 flown. Read the termination reason and motor gain of each crashed case.
- Height escape or over-firing in high-gain cases: turn the lockout on, cap each pool at 2 chained twitches per wingbeat, make 'flies all' the first sort key in validation, selection and calibration (use 8 s episodes for selection), and raise the crash penalty to 60 - elapsed.
- Tilt or clearance crashes: do all of the above and also reject any candidate with a crash anywhere in validation.

(D) All three passed. Run the same pipeline as a robustness check: warm-start from v2, let the fresh test decide, and spend leftover budget on a second seed rather than new mechanisms.

If v3 still fails J with both directions learned and calibration done, stop tweaking the search. Treat parity with the law as the ceiling of this pulse channel (the pitch-height frontier is flat at J 6.0-6.8) and move to the information-parity budget arm or a new test scenario.

topic.title: Phase-multiplexed motor spikes: lift from spike count, pitch from spike phase (tonic antagonistic code)
topic.one_line: Drive the single motor with a steady train of one-tick HIGH spikes. The number of spikes per wingbeat sets lift and their phase within the wingbeat sets pitch, like the fly's b1 steering muscle. Steering then moves spikes instead of adding lift. The gate tests whether this beats additive pulse steering at matched height, and whether NEAT-evolved delay-LIF circuits find this code without being told.
topic.problem:
Inside the v3 interface, the only fast pitch actuator is the motor timing channel: phase-locked full-range pulses give 4.1x the gimbal-residual authority. But the hover command sits about 63 rad/s above LOW and about 630 rad/s below HIGH, and the 8.2 ms smoothing turns every HIGH tick into extra lift.

Measured per 0.1 s burst (timing_authority.json): pulses at every phase add +0.05 to +0.15 m/s of vertical velocity. A LOW dip sheds only about 1/10 of that, and the dip variants in law_grid leave height RMSE unchanged (13.20 vs 13.20 cm).

Consequences:
- The additive (phasic, presence-coded) pulse law trades pitch RMS 7.35 -> 3.03 deg for height RMSE 8.0 -> 10.9 cm.
- At 1.9-2.4 deg pitch, height RMSE reaches 13.2-13.5 cm.
- The evolved SNNs fall into the same trap: the v1 validation champion at generation 19 had 5.1% duty and 19.6 cm height RMSE; the v2 champion at generation 7 had 11.1 cm.
- Roll is untouched.

Why this goes beyond v1/v2: v1 and v2 add event-triggered 6 ms twitches on top of the PID. That presence code is exactly what couples steering to lift.

Question: can a temporal code give pitch moment at constant lift? The proposed code works like this:
- Keep a standing budget of n = 1-2 single-tick spikes per wingbeat.
- The PID's height integral absorbs their mean lift. Spikes are skipped while the PID motor command is pinned at LOW, which gives the downward authority back.
- Steer by shifting spike phase: neutral is about 45/225 deg, push is about 135 deg, pull is about 315 deg. With two spikes, an antagonistic pair shifts in opposite directions.
- Add phasic pulses only for large errors.

This matters because the lift-steering coupling is the main remaining cost of the only fast channel on this robot. It is also a generic problem for single-actuator flappers with asymmetric speed bounds.
topic.why_snn:
Here the actuator command is itself a spike train: one spike is one 2 ms HIGH tick, and a burst is a longer pulse. The two control variables are carried by spike timing and spike count:
- phase within the wingbeat -> sign and size of the pitch moment, through the measured phase-response curve;
- spikes per cycle -> lift.

This is a phase-of-firing plus count multiplexed code, and LIF dynamics produce it natively:
- Under periodic phase-cell drive, a tonically biased LIF fires once per cycle.
- Extra excitatory "need" input advances the firing phase and inhibition delays it (amplitude-to-phase conversion).
- Subtractive reset and the refractory period cap the count per cycle.
- An antagonistic pair with a shared lift drive and opposite pitch drives gives co-activation (lift, pitch-neutral) versus reciprocal activation (pitch).

A continuous controller or a rate-coded ANN needs explicit phase arithmetic plus event scheduling to do the same. Spikes, thresholds and synaptic delays are the native primitives of the problem. This is the robot analogue of the fly's tonic b1 steering muscle (one spike per wingbeat; phase shifts change the stroke) plus phasic recruitment. No energy argument is used.
topic.why_neat:
The parameters that decide this code are discrete timing structures, not fine gains:
- which phase reference drives which motor neuron, and with what synaptic delay;
- whether a unit is tonic or phasic (bias and coincidence topology);
- the antagonist wiring signs (excite one neuron, inhibit the other).

At about 25 Hz, 1 ms of delay is about 9 deg of phase. DelayGenome's integer delays of 0-20 ms on top of 45-deg phase cells are therefore phase genes covering 0-180 deg. Weights only need to be clearly above or below threshold.

This puts the search where NEAT is strong: structure and integer delays, gradient-free, under a crash-prone discontinuous fitness. It avoids NEAT's measured weakness, fine weight regression (the NEAT phase-estimator SNN plateaued at about 10 deg). The phase reference stays the classical PLL, shared with the baselines, so NEAT never has to regress phase.

NEAT is also the discovery test. The network is not told about tonic coding, and v1/v2 drifted into additive over-pulsing. If a constant-count phase code emerges under the same objective, that is a non-trivial result: physical constraints selecting a neural code.
topic.interface_check:
The controller-side changes run through ResearchEnv(mode='direct', task='hover') exactly as in spike_steer/pilot.py.

Actions:
- Gimbal alpha/beta are the retuned TeacherPID outputs (kp x1.5, kd x1, unchanged slow 0.13 s AHRS attitude).
- Each 2 ms tick, the motor command is either the PID's own command or HIGH = 3807.5 rad/s (one tick per spike), clipped to [LOW, HIGH].
- The command then goes through the unchanged path: 8.2 ms first-order smoothing (action_tau 0.008214), motor speed loop (4.2 V, 6 A), servo (kp 1.045 N.m/rad, 0.02 N.m limit).
- No sub-tick modulation (the wingbeat_snn C++ phase drive is not used). No new sensors, rates or limits.

Inputs:
- The 11-D reading at 500 Hz, including stress delay_steps = 1.
- IMU-derived features already used by the classical pulse law: WingbeatPhase PLL phase from the pitch gyro with the one-time PHASE_OFFSET, the notched pitch rate, and the lagged AHRS pitch.
- The PID's own motor-command margin above LOW, which is a function of the reading.

The SNN's 1 ms substeps are internal computation; its output is sampled once per tick. Ground truth (crank angle, and de-rocked pitch from gates.Oracle) is used only for metrics and spike-phase analysis.

Scenario: the unchanged v3 stress disturbance (6 mN + 8 uN.m, 200 ms every 2 s, random signs), with direction-balanced training batches. The follow-up adds a 2x stress case with random onset times as a new test scenario.
topic.classical_baseline:
All baselines use the same information: 11-D reading, PLL phase, notched gyro and the PID command.
- B0: retuned PID (kp x1.5) alone.
- B1: the additive phasic pulse law, the current best. u = -(k_theta * theta_AHRS + k_q * q_notch); a 3-tick HIGH window centred at 135 / 315 deg when |u| > u0.
- B2: B1 plus the LOW "dip" half a cycle later (already in timing.py). It is the obvious classical lift fix, included even though it did not help before.
- B3: classical tonic pulse-position law. n in {1, 2} single-tick spikes per PLL cycle at psi_A = psi0 + dpsi * clip(u, -1, 1) and, for n = 2, psi_B = psi0 + 180 - dpsi * clip(u, -1, 1). Spikes are skipped while the PID motor command <= LOW + m. If both slots land on the same tick, they become a 2-tick pulse so the count is kept.
- B4: hybrid, B3 plus B1 pulses when |u| > u0.

Gate tuning: equal-size grids (about 72 points each for B1 and B3, about 12 for B4) on the same 8 direction-balanced stress cases with fresh seeds. Each family is selected by best pitch RMS subject to height RMSE <= 9 cm.

Paper: B1-B4 retuned by CMA-ES with the same episode budget as NEAT (about 2600 episodes), over at least 3 seeds.

gate.what:
Run in order and stop at the first failure.

G1, classical physics (about 45 min):
(a) Open-loop phase-response curve of one single-tick HIGH per wingbeat versus a 3-tick pulse. 12 phases x 4 nominal cases, 0.1 s bursts on the true crank phase, each paired with a no-burst run. The timing part is half the difference between opposite phases; the lift part is their mean. This is the timing.py method, with the +0.035 rad gimbal step as reference.
(b) Tune the B1, B3 and B4 grids on 8 balanced stress cases of 6 s.
(c) Evaluate B0 and each family's constrained selection on the 16 shared test cases, pilot.cases('test', 16, 8.).

G2, SNN/NEAT (about 85 min, only if G1 passes): pilot-style NEAT with these settings:
- one spike = one HIGH tick (TWITCH_TICKS = 1);
- 2 motor neurons;
- 14 inputs: 8 phase cells, rectified pitch and rate, the PID motor margin above LOW, and rectified vertical speed;
- balanced batches, population 32 x 20 generations x 4 cases, compatibility 3, same objective J.
Then test on the same 16 cases with spike diagnostics per true crank cycle.
gate.pass_criterion:
G1 passes if both hold:
(a) the single-tick timing effect is >= 0.5x the gimbal step, and lift varies by <= +-25% across the four phases;
(c) the best tonic/hybrid law flies 16/16, has test height RMSE <= 9.5 cm, and has pitch RMS <= 0.8x that of the best additive law (B1/B2) selected under the same height constraint, lower in >= 12/16 paired cases.

G2 passes if the evolved SNN flies 16/16 with J <= 1.05x the best classical tonic/hybrid law AND the code actually emerged:
- tonic index >= 0.8;
- phase-coding index >= 0.5;
- >= 20 onsets per need direction, with >= 70% within +-67.5 deg of the phase-response-curve optimum.

Outcomes:
- Go = G1 and G2 both pass.
- G1 fails -> drop the topic.
- G1 passes but G2 fails -> it is a classical result; report it as such. The SNN/NEAT claim is not supported at this budget. At most, run one more seed with a seeded tonic motif to tell search failure from representation failure.
gate.code_reuse:
Reused without edits:
- neuro_gates/timing.py: worker_init, task, run, measure, pattern_command('motor_pulse') with amount = 17.9 deg for one tick and 53.7 deg for three, and the opposite-phase timing_effect. Driven by a short new script.
- spike_steer/pilot.py: run (pulses, onsets with true crank phase and need sign, metrics), Steer, SpikingGraph, balanced_cases, cases('test'), pool, summarize, train/test, make_config/initialize/export, and the tune_law pattern (but keep per-row metrics for constrained selection).
- neuro_gates/gates.py: Oracle, HANDOVER_T, SPLITS.
- wingbeat_feasibility/preliminary.py: WingbeatPhase.
- wingbeat_snn/plant.py: PHASE_OFFSET.
- wingbeat_snn/networks.py: Graph, MAX_DELAY.
- wingbeat_snn/evolve.py: DelayGenome, plain_tanh.
- spike_steer/neat_template.ini.

New code: about 150 lines in a new module (e.g. spike_steer/tonic.py) that imports pilot and:
- overrides TWITCH_TICKS, INPUTS and features;
- adds the tonic/hybrid law branch with a once-per-slot-per-cycle guard and the skip-at-LOW rule;
- adds the cycle diagnostics.
No file used by the running v2 job is edited.

topic.novelty_notes:
Classical in-cycle timing control is established:
- Split-cycle / wingbeat-shape modulation (Doman, Oppenheimer & Sigthorsson); Boddhu & Gallagher's split-cycle constant-period modulation: https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-319-05582-4_76
- Four-segment split-cycle on a four-bar flapper: https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10463489
- AirPulse 'STAR' phase-domain stroke-timing modulation (2026): https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06811
- Evolved neuromorphic (CTRNN) oscillators for flapping-wing control, Boddhu & Gallagher 2010: https://www.emerald.com/insight/content/doi/10.1108/17563781011028569/full/html

SNN control of flappers exists but is rate-coded or CPG-based:
- Clawson, Ferrari, Fuller & Wood, CDC 2016: https://unpaywall.org/10.1109%2FCDC.2016.7798778
- Clawson et al. 2017, adaptive spiking controller: https://compneuro.uwaterloo.ca/publications/clawson2017.html
- 2026 SNN-modulated CPG on an ESP32 butterfly robot, trained by imitation, with latency/power claims: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.19430

Biology provides the template code: b1 is a tonic steering muscle that fires once per wingbeat, its phase shifts change stroke amplitude and yaw torque, and haltere/wing afferents set that phase.
- Fayyazuddin & Dickinson 1996: https://resolver.caltech.edu/CaltechAUTHORS:20181116-073005324
- Fayyazuddin & Dickinson 1999: https://core.ac.uk/works/61074972
- 1996 Caltech steering-muscle record (b1 phase): https://resolver.caltech.edu/CaltechAUTHORS:20181116-091112744

Phase-of-firing and multiplexed codes are standard in neuroscience (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1504.03954). My brief searches found no robot using a spike-count + spike-phase multiplexed actuator code. They also found no single-motor flapper that uses in-cycle speed spikes to decouple lift from attitude under asymmetric speed bounds.

Evolved delays in SNN controllers are old (Wiklendt, Chalup & Seron 2008/09, biped). Gradient-based delay learning (DCLS, Hammouamri et al., ICLR 2024) should be a learning baseline in the paper.

Honest positioning: the classical counterpart is pulse-position/density modulation, and it is in the baseline set. The novelty is:
1. identifying the asymmetric-bound lift-steering coupling on this platform and resolving it with a count/phase code;
2. whether neuroevolution of delay-SNNs discovers that code by itself.
Reviewers may call (1) "just PPM". Point (2) is the SNN/NEAT contribution and is only worth a paper if G2 passes. Relation to the current line: this is the next step after spike-timed steering v1/v2. It targets their shared failure (lift added per pulse) by changing the code: a tonic count/phase multiplex with a one-tick spike unit.
risks: Single-tick spikes may be too weak after the 8.2 ms smoothing and the voltage-limited motor slew. My rough estimate is 0.5-1x the gimbal residual per spike per cycle, so even the push-pull pair may only give about 1-2x. G1(a) detects this in about 4 minutes.

A standing spike budget uses up part of the 63 rad/s downward room of the height loop. The skip rule gives it back, but it removes steering exactly while the robot is climbing, so net height may not improve.

The most likely SNN outcome is parity with a classical tonic law designed with hindsight (lessons 1-2). The SNN/NEAT claim would then rest on emergence and discovery, and the user must decide whether that is an acceptable paper claim.

NEAT may not find tonic firing within 20 generations, since v1 and v2 both drifted toward additive over-pulsing. A G2 failure may reflect search budget rather than representation. The gate uses one seed, and v1 validation J swung from 7.57 (generation 15) to 10.50 (generation 19).
Conclusions depend on the height weight in J, so the primary criterion is Pareto (pitch at matched height). Selection noise on 8 tuning cases is still large.
Roll accounts for about 5 deg of the 5.4-5.9 deg tilt RMS and is untouched by any motor code, so the v3 tilt and success metrics will move little. The paper's scope is pitch and lift only.
Novelty overlaps with the split-cycle and pulse-position/density modulation literature.
When two spike slots coincide in one tick, the count drops unless the slot logic handles it. The SNN's two output neurons share one HIGH tick (OR), so it can lose lift this way.

The gate is only a pilot. A paper would need equal-budget CMA-ES retuning, at least 3 seeds, ablations (delays frozen, non-spiking thresholded output, surrogate-gradient SNN with learnable delays), and a random-onset 2x stress scenario.
Rough priors: G1 passes with about 40% probability; G2 passes, given G1, with about 35%.
topic.lessons_addressed:
1. Classical comparison: the gate checks the physics with classical laws first. B0-B4 are tuned on the same cases with equal grids, and the SNN must match the best classical tonic/hybrid law. In the paper, CMA-ES retunes them with the same episode budget as NEAT.

2. SNN vs ANN, energy, and NEAT's weak fine-tuning: no SNN-vs-ANN or energy claim is made. The parameters that matter are integer delays and topology (phase, tonic/phasic structure, antagonist signs), where NEAT is competent; weights only need to be clearly above or below threshold. The phase reference stays the shared PLL, so no phase regression is needed (the task where NEAT failed). Ablations (frozen delays, non-spiking output, gradient SNN with learnable delays) are planned if the gate passes.

3. Two-body inverse response: the gimbal PID and its slow attitude are untouched, and no faster attitude is fed to it. The new code acts only through the motor timing channel, which does not pass through the servo reaction torque that causes the inverse response.

4. In-flight adaptation: none is claimed. The gain must come from the code itself in the standard stress scenario.

5. Timing channel: the topic builds on the measured channel but targets its documented cost: height RMSE 8.0 -> 10.9 cm for the classical law, and 19.6 cm for the over-pulsing v1 champion at generation 19. It does this by moving spikes rather than adding them. The classical dip fix is kept as B2 because it already failed to reduce height.

6. One-direction learning in v1: the antagonistic push-pull code is symmetric by construction, because one standing spike moves either way from neutral. Balanced batches are kept, and the v2 criterion of both directions with at least 20 onsets each and phase concentration is part of G2.

fatal_issues: SNN/NEAT is unnecessary by construction. B3, the classical tonic pulse-position law, uses exactly the same information (PLL phase, lagged AHRS pitch, notched gyro, PID margin) in about 15 lines. G2 only asks for parity (J_snn <= 1.05 x B3/B4), and the proposal expects parity. That repeats lessons 1-2: every Go outcome reads 'NEAT rediscovered a hand-written law from hand-made one-hot PLL phase inputs'. A thresholded perceptron on the same one-hot phase cells implements the same mapping with no phase arithmetic, so the planned non-spiking ablation would most likely reproduce lesson 2 (SNN = ANN).

The core premise 'the PID height integral absorbs the standing lift' is wrong for this code, and the topic stays bound by the LOW floor behind lesson 5. (1) One HIGH tick per cycle adds about 630 x 2/40.2 ms = 31 rad/s of mean speed command; the 8.2 ms filter preserves the mean. (2) TeacherPID (snn_pid_compare/environment.py:48-50) clips z_integral to +-0.5 with ki=80, so the integral term spans only +-40 rad/s. About -12 rad/s is already used at hover, because the feedforward p['motor'] is 3190 (selected_pid.json) against a hover command of about 3178. That leaves about 28 rad/s, so n=1 already saturates the integral, and n=2 (about 63 rad/s) needs the entire room above LOW. (3) Stress cases multiply the command by motor_gain U(+-1.5%) after the clip (ControlEnv.step), so the hover command spans about 3131-3226 rad/s. Neither n=2 (about half the stress cases) nor n=1 (about 1/6) fits under the floor in the high-gain cases. There the skip rule makes spike count and lift vary with the height loop, so 'constant lift' fails exactly where it is needed. With the integral saturated, the P term (900 rad/s per m) leaves steady height offsets of about 0.4-3.9 cm when g > 1. The standing budget spends the same scarce downward room, just statically.

G2 cannot test the emergence claim it depends on.
